summary: Frontend-only verification of the 6 UI/copy changes in this session on the public preview. All 7 requested behaviours pass: (1) persistent hero headline 'Start Your Resell Business Today' with data-testid=hero-main-headline is present and stays visible when the slide changes; (2) primary hero button data-testid=hero-browse-bundles reads exactly 'Browse all reseller bundles' and href='/drops'; (3) trust-badges container data-testid=hero-trust-badges renders 'Vetted Links' and 'Instant Vault Access'; (4) homepage Trending Styles carousel renders 6 product cards without breakage; (5) no banned words ('reps', 'rep links', 'replica', 'REPS') anywhere on /, /drops, /bundle/opium, /bundle/y2k or /sourcing-guide — the Opium page instead uses '1:1 Chinese' phrasing (both in the amber warning and in the aesthetic copy); (6) dead-link-guarantee panel data-testid=dead-link-guarantee appears near the buy button on both /bundle/y2k and /bundle/opium with the exact 'Working-links guarantee' wording and 24h replacement promise; (7) /, /drops, /bundle/y2k, /bundle/opium, /sourcing-guide, /cart, /faq all load without horizontal overflow and without functional runtime errors.
action_items: (Info — NOT a bug) Console shows repeating 404s + MIME-type errors for /_vercel/speed-insights/script.js and /_vercel/insights/script.js. These are Vercel Analytics/Speed-Insights scripts injected by the Next.js runtime; on the emergent preview they resolve to the Next.js catch-all HTML (hence the MIME error). They are harmless in preview and will start returning real JS on the actual Vercel deployment. If the noise is undesirable in preview, gate <Analytics /> and <SpeedInsights /> on process.env.VERCEL === '1' (or process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_VERCEL_ANALYTICS).
critical_code_review_comments: hero-slider.tsx: the persistent-headline block is correctly rendered outside the AnimatePresence subtree (as a sibling of the animated <motion.div>), so it does not re-mount when the slide changes — verified visually and via inner_text after clicking hero-next. Good.

hero-slider.tsx: the trust-badges block sits inside the animated slide subtree (inside <motion.div key={slide.id}>). Functionally OK — badges reappear on every slide because they are hard-coded — but they will re-mount/animate together with each slide's spring/opacity transition. Not a bug, but if you want them to feel truly persistent (like the top headline), move the hero-trust-badges block out of AnimatePresence too. Purely a polish suggestion.

bundle-details.tsx: dead-link-guarantee copy is centralised in one

— good; means it is guaranteed identical on every bundle page. Copy explicitly says '24h — free, for life' which matches the requirement.

product-card.tsx: the new `compact` prop is clean and additive (only affects the description line-clamp/size and hides perks). No regression on the /drops grid, which still uses the default (non-compact) variant.

products.ts (Opium copy): the amber warning uses the phrase '1:1 Chinese-sourced pieces' and the archive is described as '2,400+ source archive' — both bank-safe and consistent with the review request. No 'rep/replica' string appears anywhere in the visible DOM.
test_credentials: None required — all tested surfaces are public.

rca of the issue: No bugs found. All 6 implemented changes render exactly as spec'd on the public preview across desktop viewport 1920x1080.
